correctness.rationale: The three normalized Hardy kernels span the degree-three finite-Blaschke model space, and the Cauchy double alternant gives det G=product_{i<j} rho(ai,aj)^2. The angle pair can be parameterized by center u and half-gap t in [0,pi/2]; the exact two-radii ratio Q_A(cos u)/Q_C(cos u) satisfies the algebraic reflected comparison R(cos u)<=R(-1), strict at the interior optimum. The remaining F(c)=q(1-c^2)/(h+q(1-c^2))*[(A+bc)/(C+bc)]^2 on 0<=c<=1 has F'(0)>0, F(1)=0, and a unique critical point because the left side of its stationarity equation increases and the right decreases. Writing epsilon=1-r^2 and delta=1-c^2, the stationarity equation yields delta^2~epsilon*(1+s)^4/[8s(1-s^2)], giving theta~epsilon^(1/4) and the displayed first-order maximum. Independent direct numerical Gram/distance grids across mixed radii and near-boundary asymptotics agree; those grids are not a global proof.
